messages:
maya: Seeing a flurry of fabric alerts in eu-west starting ~08:08 UTC — multiple GPU pools reporting transient NAT gateway saturation. some serving-runtime pods returning 503s :grimacing:

pagerbot: [AUTOMATED] Alert: fabric.egress.nat_saturation - severity: high - triggers: 6 - region: eu-west

adrian: on it. can someone drop the grafana panel for fabric egress and pool health? link pls

nisha: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/3fG6/fabric-traffic?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west - spikes from 08:06->08:12, connection churn + p95 egress latency doubled

maya: confirmed. also seeing KV cache misses on a subset of canaries — likely requests routed to cold workers when pool hiccups. logs:
```
serving-runtime ERROR 2026-04-07T08:09:22Z shard=eu-west2 conn=2305 status=503 "fabric: egress_nack"
```

adrian: good call on KV misses. can we isolate affected gpu pools? `kubectl get pods -n runtime -l pool=eu-west2 -o wide` shows several nodes in CrashLoopBackOff

rui: pulled node metrics, one host shows NIC rx_errs spike and kubelet restarts; containers restarted -> short capacity drop

nisha: proposal:
- shift 30% of new traffic off eu-west -> eu-central as mitigation
- increase canary weight decay to avoid cold-starts during instability
- reduce pager escalation window for fabric-critical from 5m -> 2m (fast cascades seen)

maya: agree. note shifting will increase cross-region egress cost ~15% token-econ for affected tenants while active

adrian: runbook step: graceful traffic tilt via edge routing first. from router host:
```
# routectl (internal) - shift by percentage
routectl shift --from eu-west2 --to eu-central1 --percent 30 --method gradual --duration 15m
```

pagerbot: [ACTION LOG] routectl shift requested by adrian - started at 1938765450 - status: in-progress

maya: monitoring. plotting canary failure rates and latency. will hand off if escalates

sre-lead: while shift in progress, open a mitigation PR to adjust pagerflow: fabric-critical should escalate to SRE immediately at 2nd trigger if within 10m, and escalate to platform-lead after 2 mins. i'll merge

nisha: drafting PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/1423 (adding cost tag and pagerflow changes)

rui: router shift showing reduced 503s already. 503s down ~60% in 6m, traffic moving to eu-central as expected

maya: pushed a short-lived iptables rule to drop noisy flows from the offending host (non-prod only) to stem conn churn

adrian: capture cost signal; tag incident in finance dashboard (tag: incident/1938765432). nisha please include in PR description

nisha: added cost tag and note about ~15% egress delta while shift active

pagerbot: [AUTOMATED] alert suppressed: fabric.egress.nat_saturation - suppression window 20m

maya: handing off to nisha for remainder of shift and follow-ups. logging out for meeting, back in ~30

nisha: ack. i'll watch and run a post-shift pool repro to validate node NIC behavior. will escalate per updated pagerflow if it recurs

sre-lead: i'll merge the pagerflow PR and schedule a short retro. please add a short summary to #postmortems once stabilized

adrian: also create a concise runbook snippet for junior oncalls: "When fabric egress NAT saturation hits: attempt traffic shift -> check NIC errors -> apply temporary iptables drop -> escalate per pagerflow". i'll add to ops runbooks

nisha: added snippet to ops/runbooks/fabric-egress.md in the PR

pagerbot: [ACTION LOG] routectl shift completed at 1938765740 - final percent shifted: 30

rui: post-shift p95 latency back to baseline, pool capacity healthy. continuing 15m watch window

maya: back. system looks stable. closing incident tracker with preliminary notes. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sre-lead: follow-ups:
- node scrub for affected host (rui)
- add automated NIC error -> early pager in observability (adrian)
- cost follow-up with finance (nisha)

nisha: will own cost follow-up and write the postmortem outline

lastbot: Thread archived by system at 1938765890
